title: Graded Euler-product identity for a middle extension
statement:
Let $X_0$ be a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, let
$j:U_0\hookrightarrow X_0$ be a dense open immersion, and let
$\mathcal F$ be lisse on $U_0$ in the coefficient conventions of
[def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], with the middle extension
$j_*\mathcal F$ of
[def-wf-middle-extension]. As power series in $t$,

$$
\prod_{x\in|X_0|}\det\bigl(1-F_xt^{d(x)},(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x}\bigr)^{-1}
=
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(X,j_*\mathcal F))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(X,j_*\mathcal F))},
$$

where the left-hand side is the $L$-series [d-real-cohom] of the constructible sheaf
$j_*\mathcal F$ on $X_0$ and the right-hand side is its graded form
in the compact-support convention of
[def-weil-ordinary-compact-cohomology].

proof.text: Put $K=j_*\mathcal F$, the constructible sheaf in the statement, viewed in degree zero. In the finite-stage pair category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], choose a representative $(E,K_E)$ and an integral lattice of $K_E$. Its reductions $K_n$ are bounded constructible, with a common cohomological interval, by [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Clause (ii) of [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin] gives an etale complex and a comparison isomorphism for each $K_n$; choose and retain these as the explicit etale-origin witnesses. The compactification and graph maps appearing in the trace formula are separated finite-type maps between finite-type $k$-schemes. The class-relative adjunction and compactification comparisons of [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class], together with the finite-Tor preservation and uniform bounds of [thm-sf-preservation-class], supply their constructible exceptional-adjoint datum as specified in [def-trf-admissibility]. All targets here are separated (compactifications, products and closed fixed loci of a separated curve), so the separated-target hypothesis of the preservation theorem holds. Thus the finite-level hypotheses of the Qbar trace theorem hold. We use only the constructible adjunction; no unrestricted pro-etale right adjoint or integral Weil isomorphism is assumed.

source.place: first paragraph: under the hypotheses of thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar; expanded using the cited finite-level results

proof.text:
This is the curve case of the Euler-product form of the trace formula
[thm-trf-l-function-euler-product], applied with $\Lambda=\Qlb$ in
the coefficient category [def-weil-pbc-qbar-category], to the curve
$X_0$ (separated of finite type, of dimension one) and the
constructible sheaf $K=j_*\mathcal F$ placed in degree zero, with the finite-level hypotheses of [thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar] verified in Step 1. Its $L(X_0,j_*\mathcal F,t)$ is the
left-hand side (the local factor at $x$ being
$\det(1-F_xt^{d(x)}\mid(j_*\mathcal F)_{\bar x})$, with $e_x=d(x)$),
and its items (2) and (3) give

$$
L(X_0,j_*\mathcal F,t)=
\frac{\det(1-Ft,H_c^1(X,j_*\mathcal F))}
{\det(1-Ft,H_c^0(X,j_*\mathcal F))\,\det(1-Ft,H_c^2(X,j_*\mathcal F))}.
$$

source.place: first paragraph, application of the Euler-product trace formula

proof.text: Apply the degree-zero clause of [lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints] with $C_0=X_0$ and the given $j$ and $\mathcal F$. Its hypotheses are exactly a dense open immersion into a smooth geometrically connected affine curve over $k_0$, and a lisse Weil sheaf on that open. Its generic representation is the one associated with $\mathcal F$; no purity hypothesis is required for this clause. It gives $H_c^0(X,j_*\mathcal F)=0$. This is the support argument in the source: a section of the ordinary direct image is determined on $U$; a nonzero lisse section there cannot vanish on a nonempty open, so cannot have proper support on the affine curve. Consequently its degree-zero determinant is the determinant of the identity on the zero vector space, namely $1$. Substituting this into Step 2 proves the displayed identity.

source.place: second paragraph: removing the degree-zero factor

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q156-12d48e0d6 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole delivery and wrote review.md; I made no fixes. The statement matches the main-20261015 and master blueprint text word for word, and there is no blueprint_update to follow. It creates no new nodes, so the rules for new nodes (B, D1-D2) do not apply. Step 1 meets the finite-level hypotheses of thm-trf-grothendieck-lefschetz-qbar, which are those of thm-trf-trace-formula-e for each K_n. Clause (ii) of lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin gives the etale-origin witness (L, alpha) of def-weil-pbc-etale-origin-witness for the intrinsic D^b_c of def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility. Admissibility is a theorem by def-trf-admissibility, thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class and thm-sf-preservation-class; the graph and fixed-locus targets are separated. Step 2 is clause (3) of thm-trf-l-function-euler-product (dim <= 1, a sheaf in degree 0, e_x = d(x)). Step 3 takes the H_c^0 = 0 clause of lem-a1-middle-extension-endpoints, whose hypotheses match: dense open in a smooth geometrically connected affine curve, lisse Weil F, U connected, and the purity clause unused. It is the unit's own step-2 fact, so I accept the declared tool use. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. There is no cycle: I checked the transitive closures of all 13 cited ids. The only off-route unit is sk-l-dl-a1-endpoints, which is declared. cor-rp-euler-product is the special case j = id, not a duplicate. No SGA source is used. Small cases agree: A^1 with constant Qlb gives 1/(1-qt); a nontrivial Kummer sheaf j_*L_chi gives 1 = 1; j = id works; a proper curve is excluded by the affine hypothesis. One point for the maintainer, not counted against this delivery: that j_*F is a constructible Weil object in the Qlb category is assumed in the statement and in def-wf-middle-extension. At finite level it is covered by thm-fin-open-degree-zero and lem-sf-integral-direct-image-constructible, but no node states it at Qlb level.
